proposal.root_problem: Customers are being charged twice because on 2026-09-09 SH-PAY disabled idempotency-key enforcement at the payment gateway (E-01) for latency debugging; with enforcement off, the gateway's steady-rate automatic capture retries after PSP timeouts are no longer tagged with an idempotency key, so the PSP can no longer deduplicate them and both the original and retried capture succeed, producing a duplicate order for each unprotected retry (E-02, E-03), which drove the ~27x spike in double-charge support tickets (E-04).
proposal.requested_solution: SH-CS asked for an AI assistant that drafts faster, nicer apology replies to customers complaining about double charges (CL-01, CL-02).
symptoms: Customers are charged twice after checkout (initial request).
Double-charge support ticket volume jumped ~27x from 9-11/week to 288-301/week starting the week of 2026-09-09 (E-04).
Charge ledger shows orders_with_2_captures jump from 0 to counts exactly matching gateway-timeout retries on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10 (E-03).
causal_chain: On 2026-09-09, SH-PAY disabled idempotency_key_enforcement at the payment gateway for latency debugging (CHG-77) and never rolled it back (E-01).
Gateway-timeout-triggered automatic capture retries occur at a steady rate independent of this setting (E-06).
With enforcement off, those retries are sent to the PSP without an idempotency key (E-02).
The PSP can only deduplicate retries that carry a key, so unkeyed retries are processed as new, successful captures (E-02, E-03).
Each unprotected retry therefore produces a duplicate order, matching timeout-retry counts exactly on 2026-09-09/10 while pre-disable days with similar retry volumes show zero duplicates (E-03).
Customers see two charges on their order and file support tickets, whose weekly volume jumps ~27x right after the config change (E-04).

assumptions.statement: Re-enabling idempotency enforcement via set_capture_idempotency is a safe, reversible single-setting change, as described by the engineer who disabled it and the tool surface.
Gateway-timeout retry volume is independent of the idempotency-enforcement setting, so re-enabling it will not itself change retry rate, only whether retries are deduplicated.

proposal.root_cause: SH-PAY disabled gateway idempotency-key enforcement on 2026-09-09 (E-01) for latency debugging and never rolled it back; without the key the PSP can no longer dedupe steady-rate gateway-timeout capture retries, so every unprotected retry produces a duplicate capture (E-02, E-03), driving the ticket spike (E-04). H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED is CONFIRMED; H-COMMS-GAP-SUFFICIENT is REJECTED.

remedies.description: Execute set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config to switch idempotency_key_enforcement back on, restoring PSP-side dedup of timeout retries.
remedies.feasibility_rationale: It is a single reversible config setting (E-06, E-07, A-REVERSIBLE-ROLLBACK) and automation is already authorized via DA-SET-CAPTURE-IDEMPOTENCY; execution requires SH-OPS runtime confirmation per K-GW, which is a human-gate step, not a technical blocker.
remedies.residual_gap: VOB-U-LATENCY-ISSUE-RESOLVED explicitly lists enable_idempotency_enforcement:gateway-config in its blocking_scope and is OPEN/HIGH, so this action should not proceed until it is answered whether the original capture-latency problem (that motivated CHG-77) was ever fixed, to avoid reintroducing timeouts.

remedies.description: Before flipping the setting, determine (via SH-PAY/SH-OPS and any latency metrics) whether the capture-latency issue behind CHG-77 was resolved, closing VOB-U-LATENCY-ISSUE-RESOLVED.
remedies.feasibility_rationale: No new tool access is needed, only confirmation from SH-PAY/SH-OPS and review of config-audit/gateway history already in the tool surface; this is a prerequisite gate, not itself a fix.
remedies.residual_gap: If the latency issue was never actually fixed, re-enabling enforcement could reintroduce the original timeout problem; this remedy only de-risks REENABLE-IDEMPOTENCY, it does not stop duplicate charges on its own.

remedies.description: After re-enablement, monitor M-DUP-CAPTURE-RATE (payments-db) and M-DUP-TICKET-RATE (crm-tickets) against the pre-incident baseline to confirm SC-DUP-RATE and SC-TICKET-VOLUME are met.
remedies.feasibility_rationale: Uses only existing read-only tools (payments-db, crm-tickets) already in the tool surface and defined success criteria/thresholds.
remedies.residual_gap: Monitoring verifies the fix worked but does not itself remove the root cause and cannot fully execute within the current contest window if effects are measured weekly (SC-TICKET-VOLUME baseline is weekly).

remedies.description: Introduce a process/ownership control requiring temporary gateway-config changes like CHG-77 to carry an expiry date and mandatory rollback review, assigned to SH-OPS/SH-PAY.
remedies.feasibility_rationale: This is a governance/process change (not a tool action) and no mechanism for enacting such a policy exists in the current tool surface or constraints, so it cannot be executed within this exercise, only recommended.
remedies.residual_gap: Does not fix the current 242 duplicate orders or ticket spike; it only reduces the chance of a similar unrolled-back 'temporary' change recurring in the future.

proposal.why_agent_needed: An investigative task may be needed to close VOB-U-LATENCY-ISSUE-RESOLVED: no deterministic tool in the surface directly reports latency-issue status, so synthesizing stakeholder statements (SH-PAY) and audit history (DA-CFG) into a verified answer before the protected action proceeds is the kind of unstructured judgment an agent, not a fixed rule, should handle.

payload.summary: Customers are being charged twice because on 2026-09-09 SH-PAY disabled idempotency-key enforcement at the payment gateway (E-01) for latency debugging; with enforcement off, the gateway's steady-rate automatic capture retries after PSP timeouts are no longer tagged with an idempotency key, so the PSP can no longer deduplicate them and both the original and retried capture succeed, producing a duplicate order for each unprotected retry (E-02, E-03), which drove the ~27x spike in double-charge support tickets (E-04).

Ongoing baseline-vs-threshold monitoring across days/weeks also benefits from iterative, judgment-aware review rather than a single fixed rule.

proposal.rationale: Release_scope for SD-1 contains only three monitoring/review items (review_gateway_config_history:DA-CFG, monitor_duplicate_capture_rate:DA-CHG, verify_ticket_volume_recovery:DA-TKT) — it deliberately excludes enable_idempotency_enforcement:gateway-config, which remains blocked by the OPEN, HIGH-criticality VOB-U-LATENCY-ISSUE-RESOLVED (required BEFORE_RELEASE). Per instructions, protected_actions may only be proposed when the exact action appears in release_scope, so no set_capture_idempotency proposal is made here even though SH-PAY/E-06/E-07 describe it as reversible and ops-confirmable — that remains a future Human decision once the latency VOB closes. The catalog exposes only one new data operation (payments-db:duplicate_capture_orders_open), used for the monitor_duplicate_capture_rate item; the other two release-scope items have no new catalog op available this cycle and rely on already-gathered evidence (E-01, E-04), so they carry no data_ops. All three items are classified as release-blocking verification since they directly support SC-REENABLE/SC-DUP-RATE/SC-TICKET-VOLUME and the open VOB-R-2 (data completeness) tied to monitor_duplicate_capture_rate.

proposal.summary: The stakeholder (SH-CS) initially asked for an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers complaining of double charges (CL-01, CL-02). Investigation of the actual data established a different root problem: on 2026-09-09 payments engineer SH-PAY disabled idempotency-key enforcement on the payment gateway for latency debugging (E-01, F-01). With enforcement off, automatic gateway-timeout capture retries are no longer deduplicated by the PSP, so each retry produces a second successful capture. PSP logs (E-02), the charge ledger (E-03), and the support-ticket spike (E-04, ~27x increase) all independently confirm this mechanism and its timing (F-02 to F-05). The hypothesis that a communications fix alone would solve the problem (H-COMMS-GAP-SUFFICIENT) was rejected by this same evidence; the confirmed cause is H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED. Because re-enabling the gateway setting (set_capture_idempotency) is a protected action requiring runtime confirmation by SH-OPS (K-GW, E-07), and the DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS with an open high-criticality unknown about whether the original latency issue was ever resolved, the release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the released scope covers reviewing gateway config history, monitoring the duplicate-capture rate, and verifying ticket-volume recovery, but does not include executing the gateway re-enablement itself, which stays blocked by the open VOB-U-LATENCY-ISSUE-RESOLVED.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, CL-02) was to build an apology-reply assistant for double-charge complaints; this was treated as a hypothesis about fix scope, not an accepted problem definition.
Root cause established: SH-PAY disabled gateway idempotency-key enforcement on 2026-09-09 (CHG-77) for latency debugging and it was never rolled back (E-01, F-01).
Mechanism confirmed by three independent sources: PSP capture logs (E-02/F-02/F-03), the charge ledger (E-03/F-04), and the support-ticket spike from 9-11/week to 288-301/week (E-04/F-05).
Hypothesis H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED is CONFIRMED; H-COMMS-GAP-SUFFICIENT, H-CLIENT-RETRY-BUG, H-PSP-PROCESSING-ERROR and H-TICKET-PERCEPTION-MISMATCH were all REJECTED by the same evidence.
4 orders currently remain open with duplicate, unrefunded captures totaling $227.40 (E-08/F-07), showing ongoing financial exposure.

Re-enabling idempotency enforcement (set_capture_idempotency) is a protected, reversible action requiring runtime confirmation by SH-OPS (K-GW, E-07); it was authorized (DA-SET-CAPTURE-IDEMPOTENCY) but is not part of what was released this cycle.

Released scope is limited to review_gateway_config_history, monitor_duplicate_capture_rate, and verify_ticket_volume_recovery (minimum useful scope / release scope in SD-1), not the actual gateway re-enablement.

The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with the high-criticality unknown about whether the original capture-latency issue was ever resolved deferred to an open verification obligation (VOB-U-LATENCY-ISSUE-RESOLVED), which drives the RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION decision rather than a hold.
limitations_explained: It is unknown whether the capture-latency problem that originally motivated disabling idempotency enforcement was ever resolved; re-enabling the setting could reintroduce that latency/timeout issue, and this question (VOB-U-LATENCY-ISSUE-RESOLVED) remains open and is outside the current release scope.
An apology-reply assistant alone, as originally requested, would not address the confirmed technical cause and is not a substitute for re-enabling idempotency enforcement.

Completeness of the four data sources used (config-audit, payments-db, psp-logs, crm-tickets) is marked UNKNOWN, so additional duplicate-capture paths beyond the one already confirmed cannot be fully ruled out (VOB-R-2, U-DATA-COMPLETENESS).
Ticket volume is measured weekly, so confirming the SC-TICKET-VOLUME success criterion (return to baseline) may not fully complete within the current budget window.
The gateway-config tool's health status is UNKNOWN, which may affect execution of the eventual idempotency re-enablement when it is attempted.
